newsitem.title: UK: CHINA SEEN BEHIND BIG LME STOCK MOVES IN COPPER.
newsitem.headline: CHINA SEEN BEHIND BIG LME STOCK MOVES IN COPPER.

text.p: A sizeable amount of the 106,625-tonne increase in LME copper stocks last month came from China's strategic reserve, which was also likely responsible for much of the drop in inventories last year, industry specialist Bloomsbury Minerals Economics said.

"Last year's third quarter surplus was taken off the market by the SRB (Strategic Reserve Bureau) and others; this year's third quarter surplus is being compounded by the return of some SRB copper to the LME, we think," a quarterly report said.

"In both 1996 and 1997 the SRB's inferred actions are compatible with one of its supposed aims -- to act as a buffer stock, helping to prevent the copper price going too high for Chinese consumers or too low for Chinese producers," it added.
The huge increase in LME stocks was not largely due to seasonal factors, Bloomsbury said.
"Contrary to folklore, it is not in July-August that LME stocks rise for seasonal reasons," the report said, adding that the seasonal surplus shows up in LME warehouses a month later.
The big change in stocks in July seems to be part of a pattern of big stock transfers of about 200,000 tonnes between the LME and other bonded warehouses.

Three previous transfers include a 260,000-tonne fall between end-January and end-July 1994, a 200,000-tonne rise between end-July 1995 and end-January 1996 and a 185,000 fall between end-August and end-November 1996.

"When global (customs cleared) trade balances are constructed for the period...the flows out from the LME were not matched by equivalent customs-cleared import surges anywhere and the flows into the LME were not matched by equivalent customs-cleared surges from anywhere," it said.
"That is, they seem to have been bonded warehouse to bonded warehouse transfers," Bloomsbury said.
